title: Offline Emulator SDK Onramp - Field Playbook (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a compact field-facing quickstart for using the Offline Emulator SDK bundle. Target readers are field engineers, solutions engineers, and workshop facilitators who need to demo or validate LLM-powered features in environments without internet or with restricted egress.

Scope and goals (what this doc covers):
- Rapid setup of the offline emulator on a laptop or air-gapped VM.
- Minimal sample app flows (chat generation + embeddings) that run hermetically against the emulator.
- Telemetry and smoke checks to confirm parity vs hosted responses for dev/local validation.
- Troubleshooting notes and quick recovery steps for common failure modes.
- Lightweight checklist for handing an emulator build to a customer workshop or pilot.

Audience (assumed knowledge):
- Comfortable with terminal, Docker, and local dev environments.
- Knows Redwood SDK basics (token usage, model names) but may not be familiar with offline packaging.

Prerequisites (hardware + accounts):
- Laptop with >= 16GB RAM (32GB recommended for medium demos).
- Docker Desktop (Linux: docker + docker-compose) installed and functioning.
- Internal build artifact access (S3 or artifact registry) to pull emulator bundle tar.gz. See linked artifact for repo.
- (Optional) USB drive for physically transferring the bundle in air-gapped situations.

Key concepts (quick):
- Emulator bundle = lightweight runtime + small model snapshot stub + local indexer for embeddings.
- Snapshot stubs are NOT full model weights. For demos we ship deterministic response fixtures or a distilled local model where licensing allows.
- SDK switchpoint: the SDK can be pointed to REDWOOD_EMULATOR_ENDPOINT to route requests locally instead of hosted API.

Quickstart (lab-style):
1) Fetch bundle (non-network): copy sdk-emulator-2025-11-03.tar.gz onto the machine.
2) Unpack: tar -xzvf sdk-emulator-2025-11-03.tar.gz && cd sdk-emulator
3) Start runtime: ./run-emulator.sh --port 8085 --mode hermetic
   - run-emulator.sh launches a tiny HTTP shim that implements the Redwood API surface (generate, chat, embeds) and serves a deterministic fixture set by default.
4) Configure SDK: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=demo-local-key
   export REDWOOD_EMULATOR_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8085
   In Node/python clients set client = RedwoodClient(base_url=os.getenv('REDWOOD_EMULATOR_ENDPOINT'), api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
5) Smoke test: curl -X POST $REDWOOD_EMULATOR_ENDPOINT/v1/generate -d '{"model":"demo-small","input":"Say hi"}'
   Expected: JSON with "output": "Hi — this conversation is running in local emulator"
6) Chat flow: run examples/chat-sample.js (or chat_sample.py) included in /samples and verify streaming and function-calling stubs.
7) Embeddings: run examples/embeds-cli.sh with sample doc set in /samples/docs. Confirm local indexer returns stable nearest-neighbors.

Hermetic vs permissive modes:
- hermetic: deterministic fixtures, safe for compliance demos and reproducible slides. No external calls. Good for customer workshops.
- permissive: allows outbound model requests or connects to cached KV store for slightly more realistic behavior (requires network). Use only with approval.

Validation checklist (5-minute):
- Emulator process listening on configured port.
- /health returns OK and git-sha of bundle.
- Example generate returns expected fixture text.
- Streaming socket upgrades succeed from sample app.
- Embedding index returns > 3 relevant results for sample query.
- Local logs show telemetry events: emulator.request.start, emulator.request.end, emulator.cache.hit/miss.

Telemetry and logs to check: (local file and console)
- runtime.log: look for startup latency, kernel selection warnings.
- emulator-access.log: request entries with short_id / correlation_id.
- telemetry.jsonl (packed events): verify event types above and presence of sample_id field.

Common failure modes & recovery steps:
1) Emulator won't start (port in use / missing binary)
   - Check: docker ps / lsof -i :8085. If binary missing, ensure you unpacked correct bundle and that run-emulator.sh is executable.
   - Quick fix: kill conflicting process OR change port (./run-emulator.sh --port 8090) and update env.
2) Sample responses are empty / truncated streaming
   - Check: runtime.log for out-of-memory. If OOM, restart with --memory-limit 4g or swap. For truncated streams, ensure client uses chunked transfer and correct SSE headers.
3) Embeddings index mismatch (no results)
   - Check: run ./indexer-status.sh to confirm index loaded. If not, run ./indexer-load.sh /samples/docs --blocking.
4) Telemetry missing events
   - In hermetic mode, minimal telemetry is emitted to local telemetry.jsonl. If missing, enable DEBUG_TELEMETRY=1 and reproduce a single request.

Workshop facilitator notes (best practices):
- Start the emulator in hermetic mode for the first 5–10 minutes of the demo so every attendee sees identical outputs.
- Save screenshots of the health endpoint and a simple generate response in your slide deck (avoid live-only proof).
- Keep a permissive-mode machine for advanced Q&A to show difference when connecting to a cached mini-model.
- Prepare two USB sticks: one with bundle A (deterministic fixtures) and one with bundle B (alternate fixture set) to demo rollouts and A/B.

Security and licensing reminders:
- Do not distribute full-weight model files unless the customer has an explicit license. Our shipped bundles for demos are either small distilled models or deterministic fixtures.
- Emulators may contain keys for demo-only API keys. Rotate them after each workshop and never store real customer secrets in bundles.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Decide on standard bundle naming and semantic versioning: sdk-emulator-YYYYMMDD+sha vs semantic.
- Add an air-gapped packaging script that verifies checksums and embeds a signed manifest for offline verification.
- Evaluate adding a GUI launcher for non-technical workshop hosts.

Appendix: quick commands summary
- Unpack: tar -xzvf sdk-emulator-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz && cd sdk-emulator
- Start: ./run-emulator.sh --port 8085 --mode hermetic &> runtime.log &
- Health: curl http://localhost:8085/health
- Generate: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8085/v1/generate -d '{"model":"demo-small","input":"Hello"}' | jq
- Index: ./indexer-load.sh /samples/docs --blocking
- Telemetry tail: tail -F telemetry.jsonl | jq -c '\n\nNotes to self (short):\n- Keep the hermetic fixtures small and cover 6 demo intents (greeting, summarize, translate, code, extract, browse-sim).\n- Wire up sampleapp to show feature flags so we can flip between hermetic/permissive without restarting.\n- Add a single-page quickstart slide to the repo /samples/WORKSHOP_QUICKSLIDE.md\n\nIf you find issues during a customer-run, file to Linear SDK-432 and ping #sdk-field with reproduce steps and telemetry.jsonl attached.\n\n-- Miguel\n(early draft; will iterate based on first alpha workshops)'
